Meet Our Founder

Dorothy Dagmar Meindok, Esq.

Law4Warriors is a veteran-owned practice founded by Dorothy Dagmar Meindok, Esq. — a U.S. Navy veteran of the Persian Gulf War. The claims process is a maze of forms, deadlines, exams, and denials, and she built this firm so no veteran has to fight the VA alone.

She is a VA-accredited attorney and a federal practitioner, and also a medical scientist. Her legal work is dedicated to representing and advocating for fellow service members and veterans, with a focus on Veterans Law — specialty and complex appeals at the appellate level.

  • VA-accredited attorney — accredited to represent veterans before the Department of Veterans Affairs, and a federal practitioner.
  • U.S. Navy veteran — she served in the Persian Gulf War, and now advocates for fellow service members and veterans.
  • Veterans Law focus — specialty and complex appeals at the appellate level, informed by her background as a medical scientist.
50States served — we represent veterans nationwide

Veterans We Help

Every Era. Every Branch. Every Warrior.

From the jungles of Vietnam to the deserts of Iraq and Afghanistan — if you raised your right hand, you belong here.

Vietnam Veterans

Agent Orange exposure, presumptive conditions, and claims denied decades ago deserve a fresh look under today's law — including the PACT Act. It's not too late.

PACT Act & Presumptives

Gulf War Veterans

Desert Shield and Desert Storm veterans face unique challenges — undiagnosed illnesses, burn pit exposure, and chronic multi-symptom conditions the VA too often dismisses.

Gulf War Illness

Iraq & Afghanistan Veterans

Post-9/11 veterans carry the highest rates of PTSD, TBI, and toxic exposure claims. We connect your service records to the rating your conditions warrant.

PTSD · TBI · Burn Pits

Cold War & Peacetime Veterans

Service-connected injuries don't only happen in combat. Training accidents, toxic exposures on base, and injuries in garrison count — and we prove it.

All Eras of Service

Women Veterans

The fastest-growing group of veterans — and too often the most overlooked by the VA. Your service, your injuries, and your claim get the full weight of our advocacy.

Full & Equal Advocacy

Survivors & Families

When a warrior is gone, the fight for their family isn't over. We help spouses and dependents pursue DIC, survivors' benefits, and accrued claims.

DIC & Survivors' Benefits

Questions, Answered

VA Claims & Appeals — The Basics

Straight answers before you ever pick up the phone.

Your consultation and case review are always free. By federal law, no one may charge a fee to help with an initial VA claim. For appeals, we work on contingency — our fee is a percentage of back pay awarded, agreed in writing up front, and you owe nothing if we don't win.

No — a denial is often just the first round. You generally have one year from the decision date to preserve your earliest effective date by filing a Supplemental Claim, a request for Higher-Level Review, or an appeal to the Board of Veterans' Appeals. We review your denial letter, find where the VA's reasoning broke down, and choose the strongest lane.

Total Disability based on Individual Unemployability pays at the 100% rate when service-connected conditions keep you from holding substantially gainful work — even if your combined rating is below 100%. If your disabilities ended your working life, TDIU is one of the most important claims we evaluate.

Yes. PTSD, depression, anxiety, and other mental health conditions are ratable disabilities when they are connected to your service. These claims live or die on medical evidence and a clear nexus — which is exactly the evidence we build with you, respectfully and at your pace.

Almost never. There is no deadline to file for service connection, and laws like the PACT Act have reopened thousands of claims denied years ago — especially for Vietnam, Gulf War, and burn pit veterans. The sooner we file, the sooner your effective date is protected.

Timelines vary by claim type and VA workload — initial claims often take months, and Board appeals can take longer. What we control is the quality of what's filed: a complete, well-documented claim is the strongest tool for avoiding the delays that come from underdeveloped evidence.
